To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed method of wafer alignment and positioning can be used to align the electrical probe with a chip on a semiconductor wafter, that the probe can be moved in a direction perpendicular to the wafer surface to position the chip in the field of the view of an electron microscope, and that the wafer can be clamped and moved as a unit to position the chip under the electron beam.
the use of the proposed wafer alignment and positioning device will greatly facilitate and speed up the testing of unbaked IC chips on semiconductor waffles.
the use of a wafer holder that permits independent positioning of a wafer and an electrically conducting probe will greatly facilitate the testing of unbonden chips on semiconductor waffers.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design of a wafer alignment and positioning device which will allow a wafer to remain clamped in a fixed position relative to the probe while the probe can be independently positioned and aligned with a chip on the wafer for electrical probing and testing.
the development of an apparatus that will allow the wafer and the electrical probe to be moved independently and then clamped in a single unit.

the development of a wafer alignment and positioning device which will allow an IC chip on the wafer to be positioned under a scanning electron microscope (SEM) for examination, such that the chip can be powered up and electrically tested while the desired area of the circuitry is being viewed.

we have developed a method for aligning and positioning a wafer with respect to a probe and then with respect to a scanning electron microscope.
